invocation: codex exec --json --sandbox read-only --skip-git-repo-check "<prompt>"   # resume: codex exec <global flags> resume --json <session_id> "<prompt>"
note: Captured in Stage 0 so the event model is designed against two real providers, not one.
quirks: Global flags must come BEFORE the `resume` subcommand: `codex exec --sandbox read-only resume --json <id> "<prompt>"`. Placed after, it errors with `unexpected argument '--sandbox' found`.

There is no system-prompt flag. `-c base_instructions="..."` is accepted without error and silently ignored — verified by asking it to reply only with one fixed word and getting a normal answer. Standing instructions are therefore prepended to the opening prompt under a visible marker.
`usage.input_tokens` on turn.completed already INCLUDES `cached_input_tokens`; the fresh count is the difference. Claude reports the two separately, so the adapters converge on the same split.

No model appears in the stream. `-m` does drive it — proved by pinning a non-default model (gpt-5.6-terra) and finding it recorded in codex's own rollout turn_context — and an unknown model is refused rather than substituted. So a pinned model that completes a turn is reportable as fact. Without a pin, codex follows ~/.codex/config.toml and we claim nothing.

`turn.completed.usage` accumulates across a resumed thread. Reporting it as a turn's cost overstates every turn after the first, and a spend limit reading it would fire on a conversation's length rather than its cost. Measured by probes/codex-usage.ts.
finding: Codex does NOT stream token deltas — it emits whole items on completion. Our text_delta therefore carries one whole message from Codex and many small chunks from Claude. That asymmetry is absorbed by the adapter, and the seam holds: a channel that concatenates deltas renders both correctly.

vocabulary.why: capture thread_id as the resume handle
one whole message, emitted as a single delta

usage.input = input_tokens MINUS cached_input_tokens (codex's total already contains the cached part); usage.cached = cached_input_tokens; ok = true. CUMULATIVE: the counts are the thread's running total, not this turn's — three one-word replies reported out 5/10/15 (probes/codex-usage.ts). Claude's equivalent is per-turn. No per-turn figure exists in this CLI's stream
